# Cell partition

The cell graph, the partition, and the geometric halo live in linkcell.
Ring membership, the Message Passing Interface (MPI) share, and ice clustering stay in seams-core.
eOn calls `pairs_within` only. rgpot builds pairs through vesin. readcon-core reads configuration (CON) frames.

This cell-partition report is generated from one log.
Every median and every interquartile range (IQR) is the value that log printed for that cell.
The raw sample line is the series those values came from, at type-7.

The hostname is `cursor`.
The host line is `Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor`.
The cpu kind is virtual. nproc reports 8 processors.
The clock reads 2400 MHz.
Virtual means the hypervisor flag is set, and the model string is the guest name.
A second node is recorded as `multi_node HOST NOT-RUN`.
Scotch 7.0.4 builds the strategy `SCOTCH_STRATQUALITY|SCOTCH_STRATBALANCE`.
The join tick is 25 nanoseconds, the measured `Instant` step on this host.
GPU status: unsupported.
The median is the whole operation, graph build plus the partition.
The part median is the partition call alone.
Commit `2053841dafb0cb4cb2a5e64c3c5550ce5345e487`.
Tree `0d85ba013307251bb10431780514db7c9ffed927`.
Exit code 0.

## Balance

The bound is `1 + parts * w_max / total`.
A weighted median gives the straddling cell to one side, so a part can exceed the ideal share by at most the heaviest cell.
The ratio is `1 + parts * heaviest_cell / total_weight`.
The same formula is used on every system.

## Cutoff and density

The mW cutoff is 4.306500 Ångströms, which is 1.8 times sigma with sigma 2.3925 Ångströms.
The TIP4P cutoff is 7.5 Ångströms, the spherical cutoff in Jorgensen, Chandrasekhar, Madura, Impey, and Klein, Journal of Chemical Physics 79, 926 (1983).
The water density used to place molecules is 0.03342796 molecules per cubic Ångström.
Basis: 1 g cm-3, molar mass 18.01528 g mol-1.
One cubic centimetre is 1e24 cubic Ångströms, so the conversion from moles per cubic centimetre to molecules per cubic Ångström uses the factor 1e-24.

## Scotch seed

Serial Scotch and parallel Scotch both call `SCOTCH_randomReset` and then `SCOTCH_randomSeed` with seed 1.
The panel log repeats `SCOTCH_randomReset 1` and `SCOTCH_randomSeed 1` for each parallel Scotch run.
One-rank Scotch and eight-rank Scotch both use seed 1.
The twelve cuts are logged because the runs still differ.

## Head to head

Times are seconds.
The pair is the median and the interquartile range (IQR) of the raw samples.
The halo fraction is the largest ghost-cell count divided by the owned-cell count.
A value above 1 means the ghost set is larger than the owned set.

One thread beside one rank.
rcb-fm leads the cut on mW-110592, mW-884736, TIP4P-1024000, slab-110592.
Parallel Scotch takes TIP4P-128000 in that block.
That one-rank block also finishes sooner for rcb-fm.
Eight threads beside eight ranks.
Eight ranks give parallel Scotch the lower cut on TIP4P-128000, TIP4P-1024000.
rcb-fm keeps the smaller cut on mW-110592, mW-884736, slab-110592.
The eight-thread whole clock is shorter for rcb-fm across this block.

## Halo counts

Each row is the domain with the largest ghost-to-owned ratio on the last method that printed halo counts, with bin widths in Ångströms.

```text
mW-110592 owned 4913 ghosts 1946 cells 39304 bin_widths 4.382538 4.382538 4.382538
mW-884736 owned 40467 ghosts 7422 cells 328509 bin_widths 4.319023 4.319023 4.319023
TIP4P-128000 owned 260 ghosts 260 cells 2080 bin_widths 7.760744 7.641348 7.760744
TIP4P-1024000 owned 2149 ghosts 1002 cells 17160 bin_widths 7.760744 7.641348 7.525570
slab-110592 owned 4913 ghosts 1946 cells 79764 bin_widths 4.382538 4.382538 4.319023
```

On the small TIP4P lattice the bin is about as wide as the 7.5 Ångström cutoff, so the radius is one bin.
That part owns a few hundred cells.
The one-bin shell can contain more cells than the part.
The fraction divides ghosts by owned cells.

## Amdahl

The clocks are select, boundary refinement, coarsening, packing, the balance repair, the graph check, and join scheduling.
Each figure is wall time.
At one thread the two sides of a join are added.
Above one thread the slower side is kept, and join scheduling is the join wall beyond that side.
A share is that summed wall time divided by the mean partition wall time times the repetition count.
The other share is the mean wall time minus the named phases.
Karp-Flatt uses the strong rows.
With speedup s and thread count p, the serial fraction is (1/s - 1/p) / (1 - 1/p).

The measured limiter for rcb-fm at eight threads is the weighted median, with Karp-Flatt 0.385.
That rank uses serial time, Karp-Flatt times the one-thread phase wall.
The first cut builds one weighted histogram per thread.
The bin count is the span of the cut coordinate.
A prefix sum finds the half-weight bin, and ties break on the cell id.
The two halves already run in parallel after that cut.
The graph check walks offsets and neighbors in chunks and reduces with a boolean and.
Packing, the balance repair, the graph check, and join scheduling stay smaller than the median.

## Before and after

The shared entry is `pairs_within`.
The public main revision stops at that entry, so the comparison uses it only.
24 calls of each revision ran in turn on `cursor`.
Each figure is the timed call after three warmups, in seconds, at type-7.
Public main wall time is 0.001669 seconds at the median, spread 0.000129 seconds.
After the same warmups, the tip call takes 0.001421 seconds, spread 0.000298 seconds.
Both arms returned 729088 pairs.
The ratio of the tip median to the public main median is 0.8517.
Ten thousand bootstrap resamples place that ratio from 0.7978 to 0.9540.
A wider frame places 1000000 points in a cube 207.5 angstroms on a side.
The same twenty-four calls ran in turn on that frame.
There the public main median is 0.279292 seconds, spread 0.018449 seconds.
The tip median on that frame is 0.261402 seconds, spread 0.004732 seconds.
Both arms of the wide frame returned 26000000 pairs.
The wide-frame median ratio is 0.9359.
Its bootstrap interval runs from 0.9071 to 0.9447.

## Rank scaling

Eight cores sit on one socket and one non-uniform memory access (NUMA) node, so they share one memory controller.
The 320 MiB last-level cache lists cores 0-7.
A timed copy of a 512 MiB buffer moves 79.179 GB/s, 76.795 GB/s, and 88.416 GB/s at 8 threads on three passes.
The rate counts the read and the write.
A temporal store of 64-byte lines moves 38.968 GB/s, 38.502 GB/s, and 39.411 GB/s on those passes.
A non-temporal store of the same lines moves 134.771 GB/s, 98.984 GB/s, and 147.519 GB/s.
A temporal store of the 40-byte pair record moves 38.123 GB/s, 41.921 GB/s, and 37.158 GB/s.
A non-temporal store of those bytes moves 132.481 GB/s, 173.891 GB/s, and 159.044 GB/s.
The 40-byte record matches the 64-byte line.
The temporal store pays a write-allocate read, and the non-temporal store does not.
On the real pair list, eight ranks move 35.046 GB/s on the million-point frame.
That rate matches the temporal 40-byte store.
Column stores of the same list finish in 0.029276 s at the median, against 0.037450 s for the 40-byte rows, and move 30.356 GB/s.
The stencil paint at eight ranks is 0.003240 s on the million-point frame and 0.040760 s on the ten-million-point frame.
The cold total still includes the mask file.
On the million-point frame the cold ratios are 1.0421, 0.8444, 0.5741, and 0.4350 at 1, 2, 4, and 8 ranks.
The reused ratios, with the cut kept, are 1.0421, 0.6192, 0.3700, and 0.1999.
On the ten-million-point frame the cold ratios are 1.0297, 0.6908, 0.4584, and 0.4513.
The reused ratios are 1.0297, 0.5332, 0.2995, and 0.2408.
Eight-rank cold intervals run from 0.3805 to 0.4804 and from 0.3918 to 0.5843.
